name: Tennessee
summary_text: The only state with a standing criminal ban on gender-expressive performance : the Adult Entertainment Act (2023) criminalises 'adult cabaret entertainment' — defined to include 'male or female impersonators' — on public property or anywhere a child could see it; first offence a Class A misdemeanour (up to ~11 months, $2,500 fine), repeat offences a felony (1–6 years). It is enforceable: the 6th Circuit reversed a lower-court invalidation on standing grounds (July 2024) and the Supreme Court declined review (Feb 2025) — the constitutional vagueness question has never been decided on the merits, a separate ACLU-backed suit over a DA's threat to prosecute a 2023 Pride event is ongoing, and no public prosecutions have been reported, so it reaches a visitor presenting in drag as a live charging risk rather than a nullity. A 2019 amendment widened the indecent-exposure statute; 7.8 killings per 100k trans women/yr, above the general US homicide rate. Below the national score 0.36.

sources.title: Tennessee Drag Ban: Rules, Penalties, and Legal Status - LegalClarity
sources.claim_summary: Legal explainer of Tennessee's Adult Entertainment Act (SB 3/HB 9, 2023): defines 'adult cabaret entertainment' (incl. 'male or female impersonators', 'harmful to minors' standard), penalty ladder (Class A misdemeanour first offence up to 11 months 29 days / $2,500; Class E felony on repeat, 1–6 years / $3,000); procedural history — district court struck it down, the 6th Circuit reversed on standing without reaching the First Amendment merits, SCOTUS denied review Feb 2025; notes no publicly reported prosecutions and that the vagueness challenge remains untested.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (HTTP 403); the underlying AP report covers the 6th Circuit's July 2024 reversal of the invalidating ruling, leaving the Tennessee drag-performance ban enforceable — the dossier's source for the 'settled/in force' procedural fact.

sources.title: Tennessee drag ban to stay as SCOTUS refuses to hear case | Advocate.com
sources.claim_summary: Reports (26 Feb 2025) the U.S. Supreme Court's refusal to hear Friends of George's v. Mulroy, leaving the appeals-court dismissal in place and the Adult Entertainment Act enforceable; notes a separate ACLU suit on behalf of Blount County Pride remains ongoing after a district attorney general threatened prosecutions over a 2023 Pride festival.

sources.title: Safe States Don’t Make People Safer
sources.claim_summary: State-by-state Trans Murder Monitoring analysis (2008–2025): Tennessee's rate of killings of trans women is 7.8 per 100k/yr — above the general national homicide rate (~6.0) — with all state rates framed as undercount floors that do not sort by legislative-risk category.
